title: 1. FinTech Eco System
subtitle: Meaning · Evolution · Ecosystem players · Types · Arthashastra in FinTech
subject: FinTech

sections.heading: 1.1 Meaning and Definition
sections.html:
Updated for Assessment Year 2026-27 (income of FY 2025-26, assessed under the Income-tax Act, 1961).

Objectives: define FinTech, trace its evolution, identify ecosystem players, and relate Kautilya's principles to modern finance.

FinTech (Financial Technology) is the use of technology to design, deliver and improve financial products and services. The Financial Stability Board defines it as technology-enabled innovation in financial services that could result in new business models, applications, processes or products, with a material effect on financial markets and institutions.

Example: Paying a tea-stall vendor by scanning a UPI QR code replaces cash, a bank visit and a card machine with one smartphone action.

sections.heading: 1.2 Characteristics
sections.html: Digital-first delivery; customer-centric design; speed and low cost; data-driven decisions; scalability through cloud and APIs; 24×7 availability; and collaboration between start-ups, banks and regulators.

sections.heading: 1.5 Types of FinTech
sections.html: Payments (PhonePe), lending (Lendingkart), wealth management (Groww), InsurTech (PolicyBazaar), RegTech, PropTech, and cryptocurrency/blockchain services.

sections.heading: 1.6 Merits and Challenges
sections.html: Merits: financial inclusion, lower transaction costs, speed, transparency, personalisation. Challenges: cyber-security, data privacy, regulatory uncertainty, digital divide, and systemic risk from interconnected platforms.

sections.heading: 1.7 Global Trends
sections.html: Embedded finance, Buy-Now-Pay-Later, open banking, CBDCs, generative AI in customer service, and green FinTech (ESG data platforms).

sections.heading: 1.8 Principles of Arthashastra in FinTech Applications
sections.html:
Kautilya's Arthashastra treats wealth (artha) as the foundation of the state and prescribes strict financial governance. Its principles map well to FinTech:

Arthashastra principleFinTech application
Kosha (treasury) must be protectedCyber-security, escrow, custody of customer funds
Detailed accounts and audit; Kautilya lists 40 ways of embezzlementAudit trails, blockchain ledgers, ML fraud detection
Fair weights, measures and pricesTransparent pricing, consumer protection rules
Spies (gudhapurusha) to detect fraudTransaction monitoring, AML surveillance
Regulated interest and honest tradeCaps on digital-lending practices, fair-practice codes
Welfare of subjects (yogakshema)Financial inclusion, Direct Benefit Transfer
